decisions.decision: Treat the following as closed and do not re-prove them: the whole M1 domain closure (V2-010 proved that stale/expired fences never advance state, that EffectFromPermit succeeds 0 of 7,784,388 times under stop, and that the forbidden-transition set matches the transition table exactly); domain-level Permit/EffectiveControl/AcceptExecutionResult/MarkExecutionLost semantics; journal fsync/idempotency/corruption rejection; real-SIGKILL journal durability (TestJournalSurvivesRealSIGKILLOfProcessGroup); ProcessSupervisor TERM-then-KILL of a whole process group with the grandchild-gone assertion (TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL); the Secret Broker's five fail-closed refusals; bounded redacted logging; enrollment challenge/replay; provider argv/parse/classification fixtures. V2-019 adds only the gaps named in d3 and d5 through d12.
decisions.rationale: Measured on HEAD 576019e with devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v: internal/reconciler 3 passing tests, internal/application 26, internal/runner 30, internal/release 3. Re-asserting covered behaviour spends Luna's context and inflates the reconciler evidence without moving an M4 completion condition. The M1 gate already owns the domain-closure claim; a V2-019 test that re-derives it would be a second, weaker witness of the same fact.

decisions.decision: Bind each M4 completion condition to exactly one owning layer and say which existing test is insufficient. (1) 'a connected Runner's process termination can be verified' = runner layer proves the physical kill is driven by a control intent, plus reconciler layer proves the Control Plane can only reach ControlVerified from a durable observation. (2) 'a partition Runner's stale Result can be rejected' = reconciler layer fences, then application layer rejects the old Renew/Checkpoint/AcceptResult. (3) 'claim, integration and promotion do not succeed during stop' = application layer through the real Service and the real OutboxDispatcher over a store, never a hand-built domain.PermitDecision. (4) 'every injected failure scenario converges' = reconciler layer, as two exhaustively enumerated tables with named-constant totals.
decisions.rationale: roadmap.md M4 lists four completion conditions; validation.md section 2 assigns behaviour to pyramid layers. Without an explicit binding, the same claim gets asserted twice at different strengths and the gate cannot tell which witness it is trusting. The V2-010 pattern (enumerate, assert the count against a named constant, partition exhaustively) is the only shape that makes 'every scenario' checkable rather than rhetorical.

decisions.decision: V2-016's real-process tests are NOT sufficient for M4 completion condition 1. A new runner test must drive a real process-group death from a control intent. Measured reason: internal/runner/control_loop.go ControlLoop is referenced nowhere outside control_loop_test.go (grep over all *.go), so its StopProcess hook has only ever been a test closure returning an error; TestJournalSurvivesRealSIGKILLOfProcessGroup kills from outside and proves fsync durability, not control causality; TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL proves group termination on context cancellation, not that a control intent causes it. cmd/runner/main.go states in its own error text that no external control-plane wiring is enabled, so no daemon composes the two today.
decisions.rationale: failure-model.md section 5 step 3 requires the Runner to ack the revision and checkpoint or terminate its child, and section 5 step 5 requires verifying that no active Lease remains. If StopProcess is only ever a fake, the stop protocol is proven against a mock at exactly the step where the physical effect matters. M4 explicitly says stop must not be bolted on afterwards.

decisions.decision: Add one additive field, LifecycleResponse.LatestMode (json latest_mode), and the matching optional property on the heartbeat/renew response schema in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml. A runner-side ControlAgent turns (LatestRevision, LatestMode) into a domain.ControlIntent, applies it through the existing ControlLoop, and the next LeaseKeeper Tick carries HeartbeatRequest{ControlRevision: applied, Processes: [{ProcessID: executionID, State: terminated|checkpointed}]}. No internal/api change is needed because api.go heartbeat writes writeJSON(w, 200, out) on the application struct directly.
decisions.rationale: Measured: LifecycleResponse today carries Accepted, AppliedRevision, LatestRevision, LatestEffectiveAt and ProcessObservations but no mode, and there is no runner-facing control-read route in internal/api (routes measured: /v1/controls is owner-only). reconciler.VerifyControl requires observation.AppliedRevision >= progress.Revision AND a ProcessObservation whose ProcessID equals the target ExecutionID and whose State is terminated or checkpointed. Without the mode the Runner cannot choose between checkpoint and terminate, so ControlVerified is unreachable and completion condition 1 cannot be met. The field is additive, optional, and pre-Stable. Fallback if product_orchestrator refuses the contract change: the Runner treats any unapplied revision as fail-closed stop per failure-model.md section 1 ('prefer stopping over availability when safety is unknown'), which is safe but terminates running work for a benign pause-intake; that product tradeoff is escalated, not decided here.

decisions.decision: Orphan reconciliation adds no new repository port and no store change. The sweep composes existing bounded ports only: RequirementsPage(afterID, limit) then IncrementsForRequirements(ids) then ExecutionsForIncrements(ids), then Lease(id) per candidate. internal/store/memory/** and internal/store/firestore/** stay prohibited.
decisions.rationale: Measured: all three read ports exist in both stores (internal/store/memory/store.go lines 141, 174, 189; internal/store/firestore/store.go lines 451, 516, 547) and the Firestore implementations are already batched and row-bounded. A new port method would have to be implemented in both stores, which pulls store-memory and store-firestore into the blast radius and, for Firestore, a new status index; UnitOfWork embeds the repository interfaces, so the addition is not optional once declared. Reusing bounded read ports keeps the whole sweep inside the reconciler component and inside validation.md section 5's 100-item-per-tick ceiling.

decisions.decision: Fix a measured non-convergence defect in Reconciler.recoverOne before adding anything else. A terminal Execution whose Lease is still LeaseActive but past ExpiresAt makes domain.MarkExecutionLost return ErrInvalidTransition; recoverOne returns it; Tick treats only ErrStaleVersion and ErrStaleFence as skippable, so the whole pass aborts and the same candidate is re-read forever. Measured with go test -overlay on HEAD 576019e: three consecutive Ticks each returned report={Scanned:2 Recovered:0 Skipped:0} err='invalid domain state transition', the poison lease stayed active, and a second, genuinely recoverable lease sorted behind it was never recovered on any pass.
decisions.rationale: This state is on the happy path, not an exotic one: AcceptExecutionResult requires lease.ActiveAt(result.At) and nothing closes the Lease when the Execution succeeds, so every successful Execution becomes a permanent poison pill once its TTL passes. That is a direct violation of the M4 completion condition that every injected failure scenario converges, and it would also silently starve lost-Execution recovery in production. The fix must expire the Lease, leave the terminal Execution untouched, and account for the candidate without returning an error to Tick. ErrOverBudget from ReserveQuota must keep aborting the pass, because safety invariant 'no new resource consumption after a hard Budget overrun' outranks completing the sweep.

decisions.decision: Close the orphan Execution hole in two places: at the source in Service.Claim (the reclaim branch must terminate the superseded Execution in the same transaction instead of leaving it non-terminal) and in the sweep of d5 (pre-existing orphans must still converge). Measured: with a Lease already LeaseExpired and its Execution still ExecutionRunning, Reconciler.Tick reported {Scanned:0 Recovered:0} and the Execution stayed running, because ExpiredActiveLeases filters lease_status == active and recoverOne re-checks lease.Status != LeaseActive.
decisions.rationale: Service.Claim's reclaim branch calls domain.ExpireLease on the superseded Lease and saves it but never touches the Execution bound to it (measured by reading internal/application/service.go Claim; TestExpiredLeaseCanBeReclaimed exercises exactly that path and asserts only that the fencing token advanced). The Execution is then invisible to the lease-keyed reconciler forever. Fixing only the source leaves already-created orphans stranded; fixing only the sweep keeps producing them. overview.md names 'orphan Execution' as a first-class reconciliation subject, so neither half alone satisfies M4.

decisions.decision: Finitize 'every failure scenario' as two exhaustive tables in internal/reconciler test code, each with a named-constant total and a total-partition assertion. Table 1 is the failure taxonomy of failure-model.md section 2: wantDocumentedFailureClassCount = 17, partitioned into convergesHere = 5 (policy-denied, execution-lost, progress-stalled, external-ambiguous, unknown), convergedElsewhere = 4 (invalid-input, capacity-unavailable, provider-transport, budget-exceeded; each naming the existing test), deferred = 8 (provider-model, provider-quota, verification-failed, integration-conflict, preview-regression, promotion-partial, secret-suspected, contract-incompatible; each naming the owning task and milestone). Table 2 is failure-model.md section 10: wantInjectionScenarioCount = 12, partitioned into injectedHere = 5 (Runner stop immediately before and after a Control Plane request; Lease renewal stopped plus an old Result submitted; Source Control write timeout resolving to success, to not-executed, and to indistinguishable; validation process hang; new claim and promotion attempted during emergency stop), injectedElsewhere = 2 (Provider CLI non-zero exit / zero-exit error envelope / malformed / empty result; secret-like fixture in commit, log and Provider outbound), deferred = 5 (Provider quota exhaustion and recovery probe; Preview deploy partial failure; docs-routing-only failure; schema migration with an old Stable restart; two-Repository capacity starvation).
decisions.rationale: The V2-010 pattern is the only way an 'all scenarios' claim survives review: an enumeration whose size is asserted against a named constant cannot silently shrink, and a three-way partition whose buckets must sum to the constant cannot silently reclassify a scenario as someone else's problem. Splitting the tables matters because section 2 is a taxonomy of classes while section 10 is a list of injections, and the two do not map one-to-one. A separate measured fact belongs in the same test: domain.FailureClass declares 14 constants, so exactly three documented classes (promotion-partial, secret-suspected, contract-incompatible) have no domain constant; asserting that those three are precisely the ones in the deferred bucket records the drift without editing internal/domain.

decisions.decision: Include validation.md section 5's reconcile-tick ceiling in scope, but assert it structurally rather than by wall clock: assert that a tick over 150 expired candidates recovers exactly MaxBatch = 100 and returns a non-empty cursor, that the continuation tick recovers the remaining 50 and returns an empty cursor, and that both ticks complete inside a context deadline of 30 seconds with t.Fatal on expiry. Record the measured duration in the evidence as an observation, not as a threshold assertion.
decisions.rationale: Measured with go test -overlay on HEAD 576019e: pass 0 gave {Scanned:100 Recovered:100} with cursor 'lease-099', pass 1 gave {Scanned:50 Recovered:50} with an empty cursor, and 150 candidates took 10.7 ms against the memory store. The 100-item bound is therefore real and cheap to pin. Asserting a wall-clock threshold instead would be a shared-runner flake generator, and validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied; a bounded context deadline is a deterministic upper bound and satisfies the ceiling without measuring the runner's load.

decisions.decision: Prove 'stop denies claim, integration and promotion' as a mode-by-kind matrix driven through the real application surface over a store: Service.Capture for intake, Service.Claim for claim, Service.Checkpoint for the one operation graceful-stop still allows, Service.AcceptResult for results, and OutboxDispatcher with PermitKind integration, promotion and preview-deploy items for the effect kinds that have no canonical operation yet. Modes covered: allow, pause-intake, pause-claim, graceful-stop, immediate-stop, emergency-stop, cancel. State plainly what is NOT claimed: no canonical integration operation and no canonical promotion operation exist yet.
decisions.rationale: Measured: grep for PermitIntegration, PermitPromotion and PermitPreviewDeploy over non-test files finds them only in internal/domain and internal/release; Service.Permit returns a PermitResponse of bool/revision/reason and cannot hand a caller a domain.PermitDecision, whose unexported nonce is the only thing release.PromotionGate accepts. So the honest application-level statement today is that the store-backed permit evaluation denies these kinds under stop and that the dispatcher refuses to emit the effect, not that a promotion saga exists and was stopped. Existing coverage stops short: TestStopDeniesPermit covers only claim under immediate-stop, TestClaimCannotBypassCanonicalStop only immediate-stop, TestOutboxDispatcherRejectsStaleFenceAndStop only PermitExternalEffect under immediate-stop, and pause-claim is not covered anywhere. Building the matrix in the application layer keeps the claim distinct from V2-010's domain closure, which is exactly what the M4 gate needs to see.

decisions.decision: Ambiguous external operation handling already exists and is not re-designed. Measured implementation: OutboxDispatcher classifies timeout, cancellation and transport reset as OutboxAmbiguous via isAmbiguous, consults an EffectObserver before any redelivery, converges confirmed to OutboxConfirmed, retries not-observed under the same immutable operation ID, and routes an unknown observation to OutboxNeedsInput; reconciler.VerifyControl returns VerificationBlockedAmbiguous ahead of any success-looking process report. V2-019 adds only the missing branch coverage and one gap: step 1 of failure-model.md section 6 (consult the local record for the same Operation ID before reading the external system) is not implemented, so an already-confirmed or already-delivered item can be re-observed. Close that and assert all three resolutions plus the local-record short-circuit.
decisions.rationale: TestOutboxAmbiguousRequiresObservationBeforeAnyRedelivery and TestVerifyControlFailsClosedForMixedReachabilityAndAmbiguity already exist, so the mechanism is present and only its exhaustiveness is missing. Re-designing it would reopen a settled boundary; leaving step 1 unimplemented would mean an ambiguous write is re-read from the external system on every pass, which is a cost and rate-limit risk rather than a correctness one, but it is inside this task's own subject matter and cheap to close here.

decisions.decision: Add runner-local reconnect reconciliation: after a restart the Runner replays its journal, and while an unreconciled prior Execution is present it refuses to obtain a new claim until that Execution has been reported. Scope it to the journal replay that already exists; do not add a workspace garbage collector and do not add an OS-level sandbox.
decisions.rationale: failure-model.md section 5 requires reconciling old processes, workspaces and Operations before allowing a new claim on reconnect, and validation.md section 2's Runner list requires that an offline Runner refuse new claims and Results. Nothing implements either today. Workspace reclamation and OS-enforced confinement are explicitly other tasks: V2-046 owns the privileged-container confinement proof, and the V2-016 Work Order already recorded that OS-level confinement is deferred.

decisions.decision: Do not create test/journeys/ and do not edit ci/components.json. Journey 4's partition segment and journey 5 live as new top-level test functions inside internal/reconciler and internal/runner, one journey per function, t.TempDir() fixtures, per-test context deadline, no package-level mutable state.
decisions.rationale: internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() unconditionally mixes ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock into every component hash, and ci/** is in all_on_change, so adding a component invalidates all 23 component keys and every committed evidence record. ci.ValidateTracked also requires exactly one owning component per tracked file, so test/journeys/** cannot exist without that edit and make ownership (part of make check) would fail. validation.md section 2 constrains journey shape, not directory location.

decisions.decision: Emit exactly one evidence record: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-019-reconciler.json, id ev-v2-019-reconciler, task_id V2-019, component reconciler, and register exactly one new entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json. Record inside it, as a measured note, that ev-v2-016-runner's evidence_key is now stale because internal/runner changed; do not edit ev-v2-016-runner and do not create a second evidence record without an explicit product_orchestrator ruling.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 assigns component 'reconciler' to M4, and the reconciler check target is 'go test ./internal/reconciler ./internal/application ./internal/domain', which covers two of the three touched Go components. The runner component is not in that target, so a reconciler record cannot honestly carry the runner claims as fresh component evidence; they are recorded as executed argv instead. Staleness is not a new cost in practice: V2-045 is a dependency of the M3 gate and its ci/components.json edit invalidates every component key anyway, and TestActiveEvidenceIndex checks schema, id, task_id and evidence_hash but never recomputes evidence_key, so nothing in make check hides or catches this. Two concurrent agents hold .agents/v2/evidence/** open, so a second entry is a merge hazard as well as a policy question.

decisions.decision: Determinism is an acceptance property. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, no dependence on another test's order or residual processes. The only synchronisation permitted with a real child process is polling an observable file or state under a bounded deadline with t.Fatal on timeout. If a test cannot be made deterministic, stop and escalate rather than quarantining or retrying it into a pass.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied on the same candidate, and the one place M4 touches real processes (the control-driven kill of d3) is precisely where flakiness would enter. GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest grants no privilege, so the design must need none: re-executing the test binary as a child with Setpgid, marker files and a bounded deadline needs no namespace and no container.

decisions.decision: internal/domain non-test files and contracts/schemas/** stay prohibited. If the work appears to need a new domain type, a new PermitKind, a new FailureClass constant or a schema field, stop and escalate with the exact identifier and reason.
decisions.rationale: The M1 gate proved closure over exactly those files, so reopening them is a cross-boundary redesign rather than an implementation detail. The known candidate is real: three documented failure classes have no domain.FailureClass constant. d8 handles that as a recorded, asserted drift in test code so the gap is visible without widening the blast radius, and the three missing constants belong to release and secret work owned by V2-021.

decisions.decision: Under docs/, change only docs/operations/reconciliation.md and docs/operations/control-verification.md. Do not touch docs/architecture/**, docs/operations/runner-local.md or docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md.
decisions.rationale: A second Luna holds docs/architecture/technology.md, docs/architecture/validation.md, docs/operations/runner-local.md and .agents/v2/evidence/** open concurrently, and a second Terra holds .agents/v2/packets/V2-021-*. reconciliation.md and control-verification.md are the two operations documents whose stated behaviour this task actually changes (the poison-pill fix, the orphan sweep, the local-record short-circuit, and the runner ack/observation path), so leaving them unchanged would create exactly the docs drift V2-043 just cleared.

decisions.decision: State explicitly what V2-019 does not claim: no Provider expansion and no self-update work (roadmap section 7 ordering); no real Provider CLI, no Google Cloud dependency, no external side effect from any injected failure; no canonical integration or promotion operation; no Preview deploy, docs-routing or schema-migration failure convergence; no multi-Repository capacity starvation; no OS-enforced workspace confinement; no runner daemon wiring in cmd/runner.
decisions.rationale: V2-019's canonical non_goals forbid starting Provider or self-update work and forbid external side effects from failure injection. The deferred buckets of d8 name owning tasks precisely so the M4 gate (V2-020) can distinguish 'converged' from 'not this milestone' without re-litigating scope, and so a reader cannot mistake the injection tables for a claim of full coverage.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/reconciler (timeout 600s): the 3 pre-existing tests still pass under the same names, plus the orphan sweep, the poison-pill regression, the two enumeration tables, the batch/cursor bound, journey 4's partition segment and journey 5.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/application (timeout 600s): the 26 pre-existing tests still pass under the same names, plus the mode-by-kind stop matrix, the pause-intake and pause-claim cases, the reclaim-orphan fix and the local-record short-circuit.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/runner (timeout 900s): the 30 pre-existing tests still pass under the same names, plus the control-driven real process-group termination and the reconnect claim refusal.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -race ./internal/runner ./internal/reconciler ./internal/application (timeout 1200s): the control-driven kill and the ControlAgent are race-clean.

devbox run --pure -- make component-reconciler (timeout 600s) and devbox run --pure -- make component-runner (timeout 900s) and devbox run --pure -- make component-application (timeout 600s) and devbox run --pure -- make component-api (timeout 600s): every touched component's check target is green.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts (timeout 300s): TestTaskPacketsValidate accepts both V2-019 packets and TestActiveEvidenceIndex accepts the registered evidence record.
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys (timeout 600s) on the final formatted tree, to read the reconciler component evidence key the record must carry.
devbox run --pure -- make check (timeout 2400s), run again after the evidence commit so that gitleaks git scans the committed history rather than an uncommitted working tree.
risks: d4 changes a public contract (contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml). The field is additive and optional and no api.go change is needed, but if product_orchestrator refuses the change the runner-side design switches to the fail-closed fallback and the affected acceptance items must be rewritten before implementation rather than patched afterwards.

d14's staleness of ev-v2-016-runner is the most likely place the M4 gate disagrees with this packet. If Sol requires a fresh runner component record, that is a second entry in a concurrently-edited index and must be requested from product_orchestrator, not added unilaterally.

The control-driven real-process kill is the only place flakiness can enter. It must synchronise only on marker files written by the child and grandchild, with a bounded deadline and t.Fatal on timeout, and must assert the grandchild is gone rather than only that Run returned an error; V2-016 recorded that the earlier form of that assertion passed even with the process-group kill removed.

The poison-pill fix in d6 must not swallow ErrOverBudget from ReserveQuota. Making Tick tolerant of every per-item error would convert a hard Budget stop into a silent partial sweep and violate the invariant that no new resource consumption starts after a hard Budget overrun.

The orphan sweep of d5 reuses read-model ports whose documented purpose is the owner read side. If the Firestore batching (30 ids per 'in' query, MaxQueryRows cap) makes the sweep exceed the 100-item tick ceiling in practice, the sweep must page rather than widen the bound, and a new port becomes an escalation rather than a decision.

Two enumeration tables encode a reading of which failure classes and injections belong to M4. If product_orchestrator reclassifies any scenario from deferred to converges-here, the named constants and the partition change shape and the corresponding tests must be written before the table is edited, otherwise the totality assertion turns into a rubber stamp.

Three documented failure classes have no domain.FailureClass constant. Recording that as an asserted drift keeps internal/domain closed, but it leaves a real gap that V2-021 must close; if it is instead closed here, the M1 domain evidence is invalidated.
